chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ahmad from Safwan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'My father and mother be sacrificed for you, some people say: Join and bring [the pilgrims] (Qiran), and some say: Enjoy [yourself] (Tamattu') with Umrah until Hajj.' He said, 'If I had performed Hajj for a thousand years, I would not have entered it except as a Mutamatti'.'

key_terms.اُقْرُنْ: Qiran: A type of Hajj where Umrah and Hajj are joined together.
key_terms.بِالْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى الْحَجِّ: With Umrah until Hajj: The phrase describing the Tamattu' method.
key_terms.تَمَتَّعْ: Tamattu': A type of Hajj where Umrah is performed first, followed by Hajj after exiting the state of Ihram.
key_terms.مُتَمِّعًا: Mutamatti': One who performs the Tamattu' form of Hajj.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Qiran and Tamattu' in Hajj according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) resolves the juristic debate regarding the preferred Hajj type by affirming Tamattu' as the normative practice, even if one were to perform Hajj for a thousand years. This statement underscores the superiority of separating Umrah and Hajj rituals, a view highly regarded in Shia fiqh for its spiritual distinctiveness and ease for pilgrims. The Imam’s emphasis on 'Tamattu'' highlights the importance of performing Umrah al-Mufradah as a preparatory act of devotion before the main Hajj rites.
